cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Lend Me the Edge
cards.instruction: Get someone to provide the one advantage you need without making the eventual success feel borrowed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lend me your good tennis racket for the final. I'll check the tension before I use it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell everyone whose racket won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The player wins. The racket meets the equipment requirement. Please introduce it as a loan, not a substitute player.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll announce the loan before you serve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the match, please. I'll return it in front of everyone. Until then, give them my name first; that's how you introduce a player.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects player/equipment credit and A5 announcement order, using expertise in sporting introductions to borrow the advantage without borrowed victory.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 credit condition causes loan label; B4 accepts and proposes pre-serve acknowledgment, which A5 defers until afterward.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants credit for useful equipment and B4 offers to use A's own preferred term.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 concession to move acknowledgment past the performance while retaining player-first introduction.

specificity.evidence: A1 tennis final and good racket establish why this specific loan matters.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 timing, public return and player-name priority form a negotiated attribution plan.
